# Cover Me

> Cover Me (cover-me.dev) is a Chrome extension for job seekers that tailors the user's resume and writes a matching cover letter for the job posting they have open. It also writes answers to the written questions on job applications: the user right-clicks the question box, and Cover Me types an answer from their resume and the posting into it. It shows an ATS match score with the keywords the resume is missing, and a check removes any skill or claim the original resume doesn't support. It reads postings when the user clicks, on LinkedIn, Indeed, Greenhouse, Lever, Workday, Ashby, BambooHR and Workable, and the user can paste a posting from any other site. There is a free plan. It is open source (MIT), built by Lincoln Laylor, and unrelated to the "CoverMe AI" project on GitHub.

Key facts:
- Pricing: a free account gets 10 AI generations to start, then 5 a week, for letters and tailored resumes, plus 5 answers to application questions to start, then 5 a week. Pro is $15/month or $35 every 3 months for up to 25 generations and up to 50 answers a day, with every application saved and searchable on the dashboard. Answers are counted apart from letters and resumes and never use them up. It is also free and unlimited with the user's own Claude or OpenAI API key, with no account needed.
- Speed: a cover letter takes about 20 seconds and a letter plus a tailored resume about 30 seconds (measured October 2026).
- ATS match score: calculated in code, not estimated by the AI. The model reports which of the posting's keywords the tailored resume covers. Must-have keywords are worth 70 points and nice-to-have keywords 30, minus 10 points for each unmet hard requirement, capped at 25. The same posting and coverage always give the same score.
- No invented experience: every skill the AI adds must cite a phrase from the user's resume, code checks the phrase is really there, and a second model call confirms it shows the skill. Named requirements from the posting, such as acronyms, certifications and product names, are removed from the output when they appear nowhere in the user's own material. Job titles, employers and dates are never changed.
- Privacy: with the user's own key, the resume goes only to the AI provider whose key the user added, never to Cover Me. Once the user agrees, Cover Me's server receives a copy of each job page the user clicks Generate or Tailor on, to read the posting, keeps no copy, and counts the site's name and the scraper used under a random ID when it can't read any page. Request this site sends the site name to Cover Me, and Report bug sends the page address, the scraper used, the error and the extension version, each only when pressed. The key is stored in the browser, encrypted with AES-256-GCM, with the encrypting key stored beside it. With an account, the resume is encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM) and sent to Anthropic only to read it and write the user's documents, and the server counts which features the account uses (never resume, letter or job text; the user can opt out by email). With the user's own key there are no usage counts, so nothing records which features the user uses. The extension has no ads, analytics or tracking, and resume data is never used to train AI models.
- AI: Claude (Anthropic) on Cover Me accounts; the user's choice of Claude or OpenAI with their own key.
- Output: editable cover letters and tailored resumes, and answers typed into application question boxes. Both download as PDFs, and the tailored resume also as a Word file. When the user uploads their resume as a Word file (.docx), the tailored Word download keeps its fonts and layout (beta); the PDF download and other uploads use a standard one-column layout.
- Answers to application questions: on desktop Chrome, the user right-clicks a question box on any http or https page and chooses "Cover Me: write an answer". Cover Me shows the question it read, writes an answer from the user's resume and the job posting, and types it into that box, where the user can edit it or undo it with Ctrl+Z. The user can then ask for a change: Shorter, More specific, Another example, or their own words. An answer says plainly when the resume lacks what the question asks about, never invents experience, and leaves personal details only the user knows, such as salary or start date, in [brackets] to fill in. Cover Me never submits the form. Free accounts get 5 answers to start, then 5 a week; Pro up to 50 a day; unlimited with the user's own API key. Each change counts as one answer.
- Applications board: with an account, every job the user generates for appears on a board on the dashboard, with the stages Applied, Interviewing, Offer and Closed. Free accounts keep the job's title, company and link. Pro also keeps the letters and resumes.
- History without an account: the extension keeps the user's last 50 letters and 20 tailored resumes in the browser.
- Not included by design: no auto-apply or form submission, no LinkedIn account integration, no resume builder: it tailors the resume the user uploads.
- Open source: the extension, backend and database schema are public and self-hostable at https://github.com/TheLinc/cover-me

## Guides

- [What is an ATS score?](https://www.cover-me.dev/guides/what-is-an-ats-score)
- [Cover Me vs ChatGPT for cover letters](https://www.cover-me.dev/guides/cover-me-vs-chatgpt)
- [How to tailor your resume to a job description](https://www.cover-me.dev/guides/tailor-resume-to-job-description)
- [ChatGPT resume prompts](https://www.cover-me.dev/guides/chatgpt-resume-prompts): four prompts that tailor a resume to a job posting in ChatGPT or Claude (keywords, summary, bullets, a check for anything made up), each run on a real posting in November 2026 with the answers shown
- [ChatGPT cover letter prompts](https://www.cover-me.dev/guides/chatgpt-cover-letter-prompts): four prompts that write a cover letter in ChatGPT or Claude, strip the phrases that sound AI-written and check every claim, each run on a real posting in November 2026 with the answers shown
- [Cover Me vs AIApply](https://www.cover-me.dev/guides/cover-me-vs-aiapply): one-click tailoring you review against automatic applying
- [Cover Me vs Jobscan](https://www.cover-me.dev/guides/cover-me-vs-jobscan): a free, open-source Jobscan alternative; plans, prices and how the two scores differ
- [Free Jobscan alternatives](https://www.cover-me.dev/guides/free-jobscan-alternatives): six tools that check a resume against a job posting for free (Cover Me, SkillSyncer, Teal, Resume Worded, Enhancv, Resume.io), their free limits, and which ones also rewrite the resume or write a cover letter, checked November 2026
- [Cover Me vs Teal](https://www.cover-me.dev/guides/cover-me-vs-teal): a cheaper Teal+ alternative for tailoring; Teal is a resume builder and job tracker
- [Cover Me vs Rezi](https://www.cover-me.dev/guides/cover-me-vs-rezi): Rezi builds resumes in its templates; Cover Me tailors the resume you already have, and a Word upload keeps its own design (beta)
- [Use your own OpenAI or Claude API key for cover letters](https://www.cover-me.dev/guides/use-your-own-api-key-for-cover-letters): setup, which models run (Claude Sonnet 5.5 or GPT-6.1 Sol), where the resume and key go, and trade-offs against hosted plans
- [How to make your resume ATS friendly](https://www.cover-me.dev/guides/ats-friendly-resume-format): one resume in six formats tested on the resume autofill of Lever, Workday, Ashby and SmartRecruiters, plus Apache Tika and pdftotext; which layouts lose text and a formatting checklist
- [How to tailor your resume in Word without losing its formatting](https://www.cover-me.dev/guides/tailor-resume-in-word): what breaks a Word resume's design when tailoring, how to edit by hand, and a tested run where Cover Me rewrote a made-up .docx in place and kept its fonts and layout (beta)
- [How I went from 0 interviews to 4 in a month by tailoring every application](https://dev.to/plain-stack/how-i-went-from-0-interviews-to-4-in-a-month-by-tailoring-every-application-1an4): the founder's job search story on DEV, and why he built Cover Me
